2867.d:
Translucent pebbles rotate over a textured background. Phase, variance, speed, range and offset are controlled from the initial has value.

Features:

Speed - The rate of change. Faster is more common.

Phase Rates - The speed at which each layer of pebbles grows and shrinks. Both possibilities are equally likely.

Rotation Rates - The speed at which each layer of pebbles rotates. Both possibilities are equally likely.

Colour Style - The range of hue values, curated around a central point. Monochrome or limited range palettes are more common.

Range - The overall size between which the pebbles oscillate.

Size - A representation of the number of pebbles in each layer.

2947.d:
First lot of Metarussia series. The Game of Life, also known simply as Life, is a cellular automaton. It is a zero-player game, meaning that its evolution is determined by its initial state, requiring no further input. One interacts with the Game of Life by creating an initial configuration and observing how it evolves. It is Turing complete and can simulate a universal constructor or any other Turing machine. This work represents a dystopian, glitched version of such an orthodox math model.

Its internal state, as well as the duration of the game, as well as the result, is determined by the input hash.

2969.d:
"Garden, Monoliths" is the result of an algorithm that started in April 2021. It was called "Grass.js".
Spring was blooming all around the house, taking over the stones and remnants of ancient battles that stood here. Inspiration was everywhere.
The initial goal was to use mathematical formulas for creating patterns inspired by the density of nature, that could be used by a pen plotter, so it kept focusing on outputting vector lines. This history and practice produced a graphical style based on line strokes, plus occasionally some transparent, filled shapes.
Each artwork will be either Garden or Monolith, for they are variations of two existing pieces from my workshop.
Each generative image allows for downloading a SVG file of the line art, ready for plotters -> just press 's' key in live mode when the computing has completed.
The "Format" feature tells you what machine size and paper size you would need, if you were willing to give it a try. A warning though, some of the SVGs can be tricky, servo-killers.
<3

'Reminiscence' specifically, is inspired by periodic nature of sine waves and repetitiveness, the recursion. While seemingly in order, most variables are assigned random values hence different shapes and patterns. However, due to the nature of waves, it still produces orderly patterns even with the random variables. Combined with the recursion which reproduces itself and particles for vagueness, the work intends to portray reminiscence.

2998.d:
There is something almost subversive about generative art that mimics nature. Rather than excelling at abstract mathematical beauty, it tries to hold the complexity and elegance of the natural world, all while attempting to be interesting art. This makes it a different kind of challenge than the mathematical attractors and flow fields that are common across generative art.

It may be ironic then that the solution to natural forms is very often mathematical. The trees in this work are built recursively as a graph, much like how one could build a fractal. But chaos is mixed in at each step to allow the shapes to vary, and reduce their self-similarity. This is a different approach to L-systems but the results are very similar.

In this token, there are:
 - Three styles of tree.
 - Twelve colour schemes (six day, six night)
 - Four shapes for leaves.
 - Five leaf patterns
 - And other entropy that cannot be enumerated.
